implementation_statement: POL-02 Access Control Policy approved 2026-09-04 (P06). Procedures for network element accounts and customer authentication are due 2026-11-30.

Workforce accounts are created in the identity provider from HR tickets and federated to the BSS, OSS, and cloud console; terminations disable the identity account the same day. Gaps: OLTs, DSLAMs, cabinet switches, and SBCs use shared local administrator accounts outside the identity provider; overflow call center agent accounts are managed by the vendor and never reviewed; no quarterly access review.
evidence: IdP export; BSS user list; device configuration review

implementation_statement: The BSS enforces role-based access (care agent, supervisor, billing, marketing, admin). The OSS and cloud tenant use role-based access mapped to identity provider groups.
evidence: BSS role matrix; cloud IAM export

implementation_statement: Customer traffic and management traffic use separate VLANs on network elements. Gap: routing between the corporate network and the management network is not filtered, so any corporate device can reach element management interfaces.

Standard users lack local administrator rights on managed endpoints. Gaps: 14 BSS roles can run bulk exports; the mediation service account has read and write rights across the CDR archive; corporate users can reach the management plane.
evidence: Endpoint policy; BSS role report; cloud IAM export

implementation_statement: The identity provider locks accounts for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts. The customer portal locks after 5 failed attempts for 30 minutes.
Endpoints lock after 15 minutes idle through device management; NOC video wall displays run under a view-only account.
BSS agent sessions end after 30 minutes idle (vendor setting confirmed). Portal sessions end after 20 minutes idle.

Remote access is by client VPN with identity provider MFA; the 2025 remote access standard lists allowed access types and connection requirements. Vendor remote maintenance uses the same VPN with named accounts.
Awareness and training requirements are in POL-05 (P06). Training procedures, including the CPNI curriculum, are due 2026-10-31.
Annual online security awareness training for office staff. Gaps: field technicians are excluded; no phishing exercises; the overflow call center's agents receive no company training.
In-house care agents complete a CPNI module at hire. Gaps: no annual CPNI refresher; no role training for NOC staff on security events; none for overflow vendor agents.

provider_if_inherited: BSS vendor; identity provider; cloud provider
implementation_statement: The BSS, identity provider, and cloud tenant log sign-ins and administrative actions by default. Network elements send syslog. Gap: no defined list of security events to log for network elements, the portal, or the chatbot API.
BSS audit records include user, account, screen or action, date and time, and source address, including every view of call detail.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Gap: no review of audit records. Planned: managed detection service with alerting on management-plane logins, bulk BSS exports, and portal reset bursts; monthly BSS access report review by customer operations.
The BSS vendor keeps audit logs for the contract term. Gap: network syslog is kept 30 days and cloud logs use default retention.
Audit generation is on in the BSS, identity provider, and cloud tenant. Gap: TACACS+ accounting covers core routers only; OLTs and cabinet switches log locally.
An independent control assessment was performed 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-14 (P07).
Interconnections with the CALEA TTP, SS7 hub, NG911 system service provider, and upstream transit are covered by contracts. Gap: no interconnection security terms with the TTP or SS7 hub.
Weaknesses are tracked in the P07 POA&M with owners and dates.
Planned: quarterly review of POA&M status and security metrics by the COO, starting 2026 Q4.
A standard endpoint image exists and core router templates are documented. Gap: no baseline for OLTs, DSLAMs, cabinet switches, SBCs, or cloud workloads.
Network changes go through NOC maintenance windows with tickets. Gap: no security review of changes and no change control for the cloud tenant.
Core routers follow a hardened template. Gaps: default SNMP community strings on 11 cabinet switches (P07); console ports unauthenticated in cabinets; cloud workload hardening undocumented.
Network elements are inventoried in the OSS; endpoints in device management. Gap: firmware versions and vendor support status are not recorded, so unsupported components are not flagged.
evidence: OSS inventory export; device management export

implementation_statement: A contingency planning policy covering IT and OSS/BSS recovery is due 2026-12-31. The storm plan covers the network only.

Network restoration runbooks and the storm plan are maintained and used each hurricane season. Gap: no recovery plan for the OSS/BSS, mediation, or portal. The BIA (P05) was approved 2026-09-04 to inform the plan.
Gap: no restore test of cloud backups or device configuration backups. First tests scheduled 2026-11-15.
CO-2 has a backup NOC workspace with read-only monitoring. Gap: it depends on CO-1 for TACACS+ and configuration backups.
Two upstream transit providers at CO-1; the CO-1 to CO-2 link uses one fiber route (P01 R-016).

The BSS vendor backs up customer data. Cloud workloads have daily snapshots. Network configurations are backed up nightly. Gaps: snapshots in the production account and region, not immutable; configuration backups on one CO-1 server.
Network elements can be rebuilt from configuration backups using NOC runbooks. Gap: no documented recovery for cloud workloads.
All workforce users sign in with unique identity provider accounts. Gap: shared local administrator accounts on OLTs, DSLAMs, cabinet switches, and SBCs.

MFA is required for identity provider, cloud console, and core router (TACACS+) administrators; cloud administrators use hardware keys. Gap: no MFA for other network element administration; no sealed break-glass console credentials.
MFA is required for all workforce single sign-on applications and the VPN (push approval today; number matching planned).

The identity provider enforces length and a banned-password list. Gaps: shared network device passwords not rotated at staff departures; default SNMP community strings on 11 switches; no process to change vendor defaults before deployment.

Customers are non-organizational users. Portal login requires a password. Gaps against 47 CFR 64.2010(c) and (e): the password reset uses date of birth and the last 4 of the SSN; the chatbot's quick help mode (disabled 2026-07-31) accepted account number and ZIP code. The phone channel uses the account password or a callback to the number of record.
POL-03 Incident Response Policy approved 2026-09-04 (P06), including CPNI breach and CALEA compromise reporting.
Incident response training for the NOC, IT, and leadership will follow the first tabletop (due 2026-11-30).

The CPNI intrusion runbook (P08) was approved 2026-09-04. Security incidents were previously handled ad hoc by IT and the NOC. The tabletop is due 2026-11-30 and a forensic retainer through the insurer's panel is being confirmed.
Planned: security incident category and register in the ticketing system, which also serves as the CPNI breach record (64.2011(d)).

The P08 notification matrix defines law enforcement, customer, FCC outage, PSAP, and state notices. Gap: staff have not been told how to report suspected incidents, and the reporting facility account is not yet set up.
Incident response plan elements are documented in POL-03 and the P08 runbook.
SBC and softswitch vendors support through the VPN with named accounts. Gap: sessions are not logged or supervised.
Drives and retired network elements with storage are destroyed by a certified vendor with certificates.

CO-1 and CO-2 use badge access, cameras, and alarms; the lawful-intercept room has its own badge group of 3. Gap: remote cabinets use keyed locks and alarm contacts, with console ports reachable inside.
Generators with 72 hours of fuel at CO-1 and CO-2; batteries in cabinets (about 8 hours).
The five-policy set (P06) was approved 2026-09-04 with an annual review cycle.
This SSP.
POL-05 Acceptable Use approved 2026-09-04; acknowledgments from all staff due 2026-10-31.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: The security program is defined by POL-01 and this SSP; the CPNI program by POL-01 and POL-04. A separate program plan is not maintained at this tier.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: The IT Manager is designated security and compliance lead, and the COO the CPNI compliance officer, in POL-01.
Risk acceptance levels are defined in POL-01 and the P01 register. Gap: first formal security risk assessment.
Background checks for all hires; additional checks for the 3 CALEA-authorized employees.
HR tickets trigger same-day identity account disablement. Gap: shared network device passwords are not rotated when network staff leave.
Overflow call center and contractor terms require confidentiality. Gap: no CPNI training or screening requirements in the overflow vendor contract.
The handbook has a general disciplinary process. POL-01 now adds CPNI and security sanctions; HR procedure update due 2026-10-31.

control_name: Authority to Process Personally Identifiable Information
implementation_statement: Authority to use CPNI comes from 47 U.S.C. 222 and 47 CFR 64.2005-64.2007; POL-04 limits uses to those rules. Gap: the chatbot upsell used voice CPNI without checking approval.
CPNI approval (opt-out) is recorded as a flag in the BSS. Gaps: the flag is not available to the data warehouse or chatbot API; biennial notice overdue.
CPNI notice in the welcome kit and portal. Gaps: partial Spanish translation; biennial mailing overdue.
The OSS/BSS is categorized Moderate (section 6 of this SSP).
Risk assessment completed 2026-07-31 using NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01); annual update scheduled.
Quarterly external scans by a scanning vendor. Gap: no internal or authenticated scanning of network elements or cloud workloads; vendor advisories are not tracked.
Risk responses are recorded in P01 and tracked in the P07 POA&M.
Critical processes and components are identified in the BIA (P05).
The BSS contract includes security, audit, and breach notice terms. Gap: no standard security or CPNI terms for other vendors, including the chatbot vendor.
The BSS vendor's SOC 2 Type 2 is reviewed each year (P09). Gap: no security review of the chatbot vendor, CCaaS vendor, overflow call center, CALEA TTP, or SS7 hub.
Gap: the CO-1 SBC runs a release past vendor support. Replacement ordered; management access restricted meanwhile.
Upstream providers scrub DDoS traffic on request. Always-on scrubbing contract planned (P01 R-027).

Edge firewall and cloud network rules restrict inbound traffic; the portal sits behind a web application firewall. Gaps: the SBC management interface was reachable from the internet edge VLAN; no filtering between corporate and management networks; SYS-10 shares the management path.
TLS 1.2 or higher for the portal, BSS, and APIs; IPsec VPN between central offices and the cloud tenant; SSH for device management on core routers.
Providers use FIPS-validated cryptographic modules per their SOC 2 system descriptions.
BSS and cloud storage (including the CDR archive) are encrypted at rest with provider-managed keys; laptops and tablets are encrypted. Gap: the configuration backup server at CO-1 is unencrypted.
Endpoints and cloud VMs are patched monthly. Gap: network elements are patched ad hoc; both edge routers have open critical advisories.
EDR on all 285 laptops and desktops and on cloud VMs.
Gap: no security monitoring; the NOC monitors availability. Planned: managed detection and response with SIEM by 2027-01-31.
Portal forms validate input. Gap: chatbot free-text input reaches the account API without an allow-list of actions (P10).

Records retention follows the finance schedule. Gaps: CDR archive kept 36 months online; SSN4 and date of birth kept for the life of the account; CPNI records (approvals, notices, campaigns, breaches) lack defined retention.
